div.l: And all the remenaunt of our pilgrymage
But first I pray yow of yourᵉ curtesy
That ye ne arrete nat my velany
Though þat I pleinly speke in this mat̉ere
To telle yoᵘ her wordes and her chere
Ne though I speke her wordes ꝓproprely
For this ye knowe as wele as I
Who so shall telle a tale aft̉er a man
He most reherce as nygh as eủer he can
Eủery word / yf yt be in his charge
Speke he neủer so rewdely ne so large
Or elles he mot telle his tale vntrewe
Or feyn thing or fynde wordes newe
He may nought spare all thogh yt were his brother
He mote as wele sey o. worde as an other
Crist spake hym self full brode in holy wryt
And wele ye wote no velany ys yt
Eke plato seith who so can hym rede
The wordes most be cosyn to the dede
Also I pray yoᵘ to forgeve it me
Thogh I haue nat set folk in her degre
Here in this tale as that they shold stond
My wit is short ye may wele vndrestond
Grete chere made our host vs eủerychone
And to soper set we vs anone
He s̉erued vs wᵗith vitailles at þe best
Strong was the wyne and wele drynke vs lest
A semely man our host was wᵗith all
For to ben a Marchall in an hall
A large man he was wᵗith yen stepe
A feirer burgeys was there nought in chepe
Bold of his speche and wyse and wele taght
And of manhode lakked hym right naght
Eke he was therto a mery man
And after soper pley he began
And spake of myrth amonge other thinges
Whan that we hade made our rekenynges
And seide lo lordyngᵉs trewely
Ye be to me right welcome hertly
For by my trewth yf þat I shall nat lye
